clue.text: Unexpected gift of touring artist?

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the scrambled letters travel around the artist
something unexpected turns up in a surprising form, so these letters come out rearranged

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the standard abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: A present left behind by an artist on tour, wryly described as a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a scrawl on a wall is an uninvited 'gift' from an artist on the move, and 'touring' doubles as the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A single piece of wall scrawl is an uninvited offering left by a roaming street painter.

clue.text: I order fish

definitions.meaning: read whimsically, one who groups things, that is, puts them in order
a large sea bass found in warm waters

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a joke on the answer as a word: someone who groups (orders) things, so the answer itself could say 'I order'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sorts things into groups is jokingly an orderer, and it is also a large warm-sea food species.

clue.text: Resort to make public broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means sent out over the airwaves, so the word is taken as spoken

parts.note: to air an opinion is to make it public

explanation.surface: A request to advertise a holiday town on radio or television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' signals a word heard rather than seen. AYR is a seaside resort town on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish town on the Firth of Clyde is a traditional seaside holiday destination.

clue.text: Crash site to use for PR, strangely

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so these letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A disaster scene being exploited for publicity, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crash site' looks like an accident scene, but 'crash' is slang for sleep: a bed is where you crash.
explanation.definitionFit: To crash is slang for falling asleep, and a canopied bed with tall corner pillars is a place to do so.

clue.text: See, it's torn up root in odd places

indicators.note: in odd places means take the letters in the first, third, fifth and further odd positions of the words

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a root has been ripped out at scattered spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not a verb here but a bishop's diocese. TRURO, in Cornwall, has a cathedral and is the seat of a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's diocese, and this Cornish cathedral city gives its name to one.

clue.text: Internet spy trap — something punters might fall into?

parts.note: a web is the trap a spider spins
the Cam is the river at Cambridge, where people go punting and sometimes fall in

explanation.surface: An online snooping device is likened to a snare, like water a boater might tumble into.
explanation.walkthrough: Punters here are people in flat-bottomed punts, not gamblers; punting on the River Cam is a Cambridge pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera feeding images over the internet can be used to watch people covertly.

clue.text: Pound something that can have variable value in time

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an era is a period of time

parts.words: something that can have variable value
parts.note: z is a typical algebraic variable, a symbol that can take any value

explanation.surface: A description of money whose worth fluctuates over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like currency, and the surface keeps that up with 'value', but it is the American poet Ezra Pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The modernist poet Ezra Pound is known by his surname, so his first name is clued by it.

clue.text: Vanishing cream lover? One catches her wrinkles

indicators.note: wrinkles means creases, so the letters are crumpled into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An advert for a skin cream that seems to conquer a woman's wrinkles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vanishing cream' sounds cosmetic, but the definition is a creature that vanishes and, being a cat, loves cream: the grinning cat in Alice in Wonderland that fades away.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's grinning cat vanishes bit by bit, and cats are traditionally fond of cream.

clue.text: European holiday by the sea that gets one out of the front line

definitions.text: that gets one out of the front line

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
vac is short for vacation, a holiday

explanation.surface: A seaside break in Europe as an escape from the stresses of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a description, not a noun synonym: a military evacuation of wounded soldiers by air is what gets one out of the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical evacuation by helicopter or plane removes wounded troops from combat zones.

clue.text: Overall, a strange consonant

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Taken all together, a peculiar letter sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overall' looks like the opening adverb but is the fodder, with 'a', for 'strange'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound such as t, d or n made with the tongue against the ridge behind the teeth is this kind of consonant.

clue.text: Building society by us used to close after day's work

indicators.note: after places close behind the day

parts.note: something used by us is ours, so 'by us' gives the possessive our
a building society is a mutual, owned by its members
Fri is the abbreviation for Friday, the day's work ending
a close is an end

explanation.surface: A building society used by us shuts after the working day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building society' is a British savings and loan institution, often called a mutual. The definition is 'work', a novel: the last completed one by Charles Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a novel by Charles Dickens, and a novel is a literary work.

clue.text: Rings back before press chief gets dismissed

indicators.note: back means read in reverse, so the rings are spelt from the end

parts.note: hoops are rings; two of them for the plural
ED, editor, heads a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss is sacked after a phone call returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings back' suggests returning a call, but it is two hoops written backwards; 'before' just puts them ahead of ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff at an idea and brush it aside is to wave it away contemptuously, or reject it.

clue.text: Break from work left one happy at last

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
port is the left side of a ship
a unit is one

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A rest from work left someone finally content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' looks like a rest from work, the surface's sense, but it means a lucky chance, as in 'a big break'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky break is a chance to get ahead, a favourable opening.

clue.text: Coarse chap's refreshing cup victory just the start.

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea, a refreshing cup

indicators.note: just the start means only the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A rough man enjoys a cup of tea after the first win.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAV is British slang for a brash, loutish young person.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a loutish, flashily dressed young person, a vulgar type.

clue.text: Prisoner taking cell mate, perhaps, as a wife?

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
jug is slang for prison, a cell
an ally is a mate, a friend

explanation.surface: A convict who takes a cellmate as a spouse, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate, perhaps' plays on a spouse; the surface also hints at conjugal visits in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting as a spouse means in a marital manner, the adverb for married life.

clue.text: One after cuts about to make comeback

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so the first pieces go inside the other

parts.note: re means about, concerning
one is the Roman numeral I
post means after, as in postwar

explanation.surface: Someone who suffers after spending cuts plans a revival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comeback' looks like a revival, but it means a sharp retort.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick, witty reply is a comeback, and so is a fencer's counterthrust.

clue.text: Get to 23, perhaps, with point docked

definitions.text: Get to 23, perhaps, with point docked

parts.words: Get to 23, perhaps, with point docked
parts.note: 23 is the Irish name that reads as a goalless draw score; dock its point (compass N) and it reads as one apiece, the score a trailing side reaches by scoring once

explanation.walkthrough: Remove N, a compass point, from the name at 23 and it becomes I-ALL, one-all: the score you reach when you level the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Levelling the score at one goal each is what a trailing football side does when it scores.

clue.text: Earl whose wife rode barely within mile of Richmond

indicators.note: within means the answer is tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An earl's wife rides naked close to Richmond.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Godiva legendarily rode naked through Coventry; her husband was Leofric, Earl of Mercia.
explanation.definitionFit: Leofric, Earl of Mercia, was husband of Lady Godiva, who rode naked through Coventry in legend.

clue.text: One coming from average beginning to another world, almost?

definitions.text: One coming from average beginning to another world, almost?

parts.note: par is the average or normal level

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Venus is another planet, another world

explanation.surface: Someone rising from a humble background to a whole new world.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines an upstart, someone from an ordinary start who has arrived in high society, a different world.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is a person of humble origins who has newly risen to wealth or status.

clue.text: Nothing left after regiment dropped Desert Shield?

indicators.note: after sends the zero and the left sign behind the soldiers

parts.note: the Paras, the Parachute Regiment, are soldiers dropped from aircraft
nothing is zero, O

explanation.surface: A military operation in which troops are dropped into the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert Shield' was a 1990 Gulf military operation, which suits the soldiers; here it is a sunshade, a shield in the desert. 'After' puts O and L behind PARAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade shields a person from the fierce sun, as one would need in a desert.

clue.text: With judge standing in for queen, again puts up the condemned

indicators.note: standing in for means one thing replaces another

parts.note: to re-erect is to put up again

explanation.surface: With a deputy judge replacing the queen, the condemned are put on show again.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen; J replaces it. The definition uses 'condemned' as a plural noun: things rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: Rejected items or people are those turned down as worthless, the discarded ones.

clue.text: Rubber for body outfit's yet to be trimmed around

indicators.note: around means the trimmed word wraps the other
trimmed means cut at the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: still means yet
a rig is an outfit of clothes

explanation.surface: An outfit is still to be altered around the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubber' suggests an eraser or a massage, but a strigil was an ancient Greek and Roman scraper for cleaning oil and sweat off the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved scraper used in ancient Greece and Rome to clean sweat and oil from the skin.

clue.text: Rake when first of garden leaves turn red

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: to rouge is to redden, to colour red

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gardener rakes when autumn leaves redden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' and 'leaves' paint a garden; a rake is also a dissolute man. 'leaves' drops G from ROUGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a debauched pleasure-seeking man, a libertine.

clue.text: Shift, perhaps, or adjust clothes line round the corner

indicators.note: clothes means dresses or covers, so one piece wraps the others

parts.note: to alter is to adjust
nigh means near, just round the corner

explanation.surface: Someone alters clothes or moves a washing line around a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' is a work period: an overnight stint is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift of work can last all night, so an overnight session is an example.

clue.text: Irishman's zanier at heart on the whole

indicators.note: at heart picks out the central letters of the word

parts.note: on the whole means all, altogether

explanation.surface: An Irishman is on the whole rather crazier at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' takes the middle two letters of 'zanier', NI.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common Irish first name, so it can stand for an Irishman.

clue.text: Obscure second book excluded from publisher's promotion

indicators.note: excluded from means left out of, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a blurb is the publisher's promotional text on a book jacket
B is the abbreviation for book, the second of the two in the word

explanation.surface: A second book is left out of a publisher's advertising campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second of the two Bs goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To blur something is to make it indistinct or hard to see, to cloud it.

clue.text: Dithering Bob pens will inside two years

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bob is old British slang for a shilling, a pre-decimal coin

indicators.note: inside means placed within

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year, twice
shall and will both mark the future

explanation.surface: Bob is hesitating while drafting his will, over two years.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin, nicknamed a bob; 'Bob' is not a man's name here. 'Will' is the future auxiliary, not a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitating and being unable to decide is the same as dithering.

clue.text: Poetic princess a real-life one reared

indicators.note: reared means raised up, so in a down answer the letters run upwards

parts.note: Di, Princess Diana, was a real-life princess

explanation.surface: A princess from poetry is raised as a real-life one.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's The Princess features Princess Ida.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's narrative poem The Princess centres on Princess Ida, a literary heroine.

clue.text: Musical finale with Australian rock bands

indicators.note: finale means the end, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: Ayers Rock is the huge rock formation in central Australia, also called Uluru

explanation.surface: A musical's closing number features Australian rock groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock bands' suggests music; 'bands' alone is the definition, strata of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Layers are horizontal strips or strata, bands of material lying one on another.

clue.text: Co-operate, quietly anticipating a song and dance

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
a lay is a song
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone works together quietly, looking forward to a song and dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anticipating' just puts P ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To go along with others and cooperate is an idiom from games.
